items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: I had a lawyer from the federal government, Will Schotten. And he said, don't worry about it, Tom.

ctx.x: Well, another time, a guy come up to me and asked me if I would play up there in -- oh, somewhere up in the northern part of Massachusetts. And I told him, yeah. I hired a car and we went up there and the man says, what are you doing up here? I says, well, didn't you tell me -- he said I got a telegram saying that everything was off. I said, no, I wrote that everything is on, be up there.

And, sure enough, we went down to the telegraph office and there was the telegram, everything off. I said, that guy was dizzy, whoever signed that. Because -- I came back to New York, I mean, to Boston and I got my lawyer. I had a lawyer from the federal government, Will Schotten. And he said, don't worry about it, Tom. I'll get -- so sure enough, I got all my money back.
That's good. You even remember the lawyer's name from that era.
